newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso stays firm at close, mkt awaits data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso stays firm at close, mkt awaits data.

text.p: The Mexican peso retained early firmness at the close on Monday after a quiet session amid a market awaiting trade data, dealers said.

"The peso did not gain strength because players held on to long dollar positions... They're waiting for trade figures and Greenspan's comments," a trader said, referring to forthcoming testimony to a U.S. Congress panel by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed the session 1.6 and 1.5 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8850/7.8880 and 7.8820/7.8850 per dollar.
Traders said they had expected the Finance Ministry to release preliminary trade figures for June, but the data had not been released by the close of trade.
A Reuters survey MEX22 of 12 financial firms in Mexico City showed they predicted an average trade surplus of $164.83 million in June.
Traders said the session had been quiet and the 48-hour peso had traded between a 7.8800 to 7.8900 band per dollar.
"The peso traded within a narrow range despite the slide on the bourse because there was no real outflow of dollars," the trader added.
The Mexican bourse's blue chip IPC index was down 109.59 points at 4,610.97 when the foreign exchange market closed.
Same-day peso contracts ended trade mid-morning 0.8 of a centavo firmer at 7.8750/7.8800 per dollar.
